markdown_content: ## FitMaps Overview (Stress, Strain, Fit, Pressure) This section introduces FitMaps and explains what each fit map represents in Clo/Cloth simulation. It also clarifies that FitMaps are viewed individually and how to access them in the 3D interface. FitMaps are available in the **3D toggle menu**, directly **under the fabric icon**, as the **Fit Map** icon. When you hover over it, you can access **four fit maps**: - **Stress** - **Strain** - **Fit** - **Pressure** You **cannot view them all at once**—you must open each map individually. The fit map values shown on the surface include a **global numeric scale**, a **color gradient**, and **units** (for example, stress uses **kPa**). --- ## Pre-Fit Setup Checklist (Pattern Pieces, Skin Offset, Fitting Simulation, GPU/CPU) This section covers the required simulation and geometry settings to ensure FitMaps produce accurate results—especially **particle distance**, **skin offset**, and using **Fitting** simulation mode. Before using FitMaps to compare garments, ensure both the **avatar** and **garments** are properly set up. ### 1) Pattern piece detail and “particle distance” - Confirm **all pattern pieces are present** and visible. - Set **particle distance to 5** for fitting so you can clearly see folding/scrunching/detail. - (Higher values like **20** may help editing previews, but **5** is recommended for fitting detail.) - In the **property editor**, verify the selected pattern piece’s particle distance is **5**. ### 2) Skin offset must be zero (for accurate pressure/pressure maps) - Select the **avatar** and check **skin offset** in the **property editor**. - Target: **skin offset = 0** (the speaker notes “0 is better”; some avatars may show 1 or 0). - Why it matters: pressure maps need the garment to sit **directly on top of the avatar** with **no “pretend air gap”** between avatar and garment. - Key related properties observed in the example include: - **Static friction: 0.8** - **Kinetic friction: 0.05** - **Skin inward offset: 5** (not emphasized as important) - Setting skin offset to 0 helps interpret pressure correctly for FitMaps (pressure on the body, not an editor-only gap). ### 3) Simulation mode: use **Fitting**, not **Normal** - Set simulation to **Fitting** / **Fitting sim**. - **Do not use Normal simulation** for fitting accuracy. - Tradeoff: **Fitting sim takes more time**. - Performance options: - If you have a **PC**, use **GPU fitting** if available. - If you’re on **Mac** (as stated), you may need **CPU**. - The core rule: use **Fitting** mode before generating FitMaps. ### 4) Optional: faster setup with High Res / Low Res tools - A **high-res tool** can automatically apply the needed setup quickly. - The **low-res** tool is mentioned as hidden. ### 5) Optional: custom view and tape tools - Optional preference: right-click → **Custom View**, then set an angle/view you like. - You can reset view alignment to confirm fitting after zoom/pan. - Use **tape tools** to draw tape on the avatar to check alignment against specific lines. --- ## Stress Map (kPa): Force per Unit Area and Fabric Pressure Interpretation This section explains what the **Stress** fit map measures, how to read the color/number scale, and the key direction of interpretation (fabric pressure on the body). ### Definition The **Stress map**: - **Displays the force per unit area in kPa** applied to a garment by external stress. - Interprets how much **pressure is in the fabric per section** due to a **tight-fitted garment**. ### Important interpretation: fabric pressure on the body - Stress/pressure readouts reflect **pressure the fabric applies to the body**, not pressure the body applies to the fabric. - Example analogy: placing a hand on a fabric panel—FitMaps show how much pressure the applied load creates in the fabric, corresponding to how tight it may feel on-body. ### Reading the global scale (colors and numbers) - Stress map includes: - A **gradient color scale** - **Numbers** and a **unit** (kPa) - The values are described as **global**: - **Red = 100** - **Orange ~ 85.7** - **Light blue ~ 14.29** - These numbers **do not directly equal** “fabric strength limits.” - They indicate relative stress levels in the map: - If the selected point shows **101**, it appears **red**. - If it shows **75**, it appears **green/orange** depending on the scale. - If it shows **9.47**, it is **low** (lighter colors). ### Practical implication - chunks.content: ## FitMaps Overview (Stress, Strain, Fit, Pressure) This section introduces FitMaps and explains what each fit map represents in Clo/Cloth simulation. It also clarifies that FitMaps are viewed individually and how to access them in the 3D interface. FitMaps are available in the **3D toggle menu**, directly **under the fabric icon**, as the **Fit Map** icon. When you hover over it, you can access **four fit maps**: - **Stress** - **Strain** - **Fit** - **Pressure** You **cannot view them all at once**—you must open each map individually. The fit map values shown on the surface include a **global numeric scale**, a **color gradient**, and **units** (for example, stress uses **kPa**). --- ## Pre-Fit Setup Checklist (Pattern Pieces, Skin Offset, Fitting Simulation, GPU/CPU) This section covers the required simulation and geometry settings to ensure FitMaps produce accurate results—especially **particle distance**, **skin offset**, and using **Fitting** simulation mode. Before using FitMaps to compare garments, ensure both the **avatar** and **garments** are properly set up. ### 1) Pattern piece detail and “particle distance” - Confirm **all pattern pieces are present** and visible. - Set **particle distance to 5** for fitting so you can clearly see folding/scrunching/detail. - (Higher values like **20** may help editing previews, but **5** is recommended for fitting detail.) - In the **property editor**, verify the selected pattern piece’s particle distance is **5**. ### 2) Skin offset must be zero (for accurate pressure/pressure maps) - Select the **avatar** and check **skin offset** in the **property editor**. - Target: **skin offset = 0** (the speaker notes “0 is better”; some avatars may show 1 or 0). - Why it matters: pressure maps need the garment to sit **directly on top of the avatar** with **no “pretend air gap”** between avatar and garment. - Key related properties observed in the example include: - **Static friction: 0.8** - **Kinetic friction: 0.05** - **Skin inward offset: 5** (not emphasized as important) - Setting skin offset to 0 helps interpret pressure correctly for FitMaps (pressure on the body, not an editor-only gap). ### 3) Simulation mode: use **Fitting**, not **Normal** - Set simulation to **Fitting** / **Fitting sim**. - **Do not use Normal simulation** for fitting accuracy. - Tradeoff: **Fitting sim takes more time**. - Performance options: - If you have a **PC**, use **GPU fitting** if available. - If you’re on **Mac** (as stated), you may need **CPU**. - The core rule: use **Fitting** mode before generating FitMaps. ### 4) Optional: faster setup with High Res / Low Res tools - A **high-res tool** can automatically apply the needed setup quickly. - The **low-res** tool is mentioned as hidden. ### 5) Optional: custom view and tape tools - Optional preference: right-click → **Custom View**, then set an angle/view you like. - You can reset view alignment to confirm fitting after zoom/pan. - Use **tape tools** to draw tape on the avatar to check alignment against specific lines.
